dedupe_keys.name: pycraf python package for spectrum management compatibility studies itu r p 452 and p 676

description: pycraf is a Python package for spectrum-management compatibility studies, written by Benjamin Winkel at the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy in Bonn and described in a 2018 paper in Advances in Radio Science. Its core is an implementation of Recommendation ITU-R P.452 (version 16), which calculates the path attenuation between an interfering transmitter and a victim receiver from distance and terrain, and it also computes atmospheric attenuation following ITU-R P.676, with further tools for antenna patterns, geometry and conversions. A typical use is the interference level at a radio telescope caused by a broadcasting tower; the authors also ran a Monte Carlo study of the possible harm from 5G base stations and user devices around a radio observatory. Coverage: any location, using terrain data such as SRTM. Format and access: Python package on PyPI and GitHub, documentation on GitHub Pages, free under GPL v3; version 2.1.0 was released on 1 February 2025 and the first release dates from June 2017. Caveats: aimed at compatibility studies, not coverage planning; results are only as good as the terrain and clutter inputs. Simulation uses: interference and coverage calculations for broadcasting and mobile transmitters, and hazard exposure of radio links to anomalous propagation. Related records: Py1812 and Py1546 implement other ITU-R propagation methods, and the NTIA ITM model covers similar paths.
